identity.name: Maona of Chios
native_names: Maona di Chio e di Focea

land.text: Chios, under Byzantine governors since 1329 (Martino Zaccaria page)

predecessors.note: The Lordship of Chios (lordship-of-chios, 1304-1329) held the island before the Byzantines retook it.

land.text: Chios, 'captured by the Ottoman Empire after the surrender to Piyale Pasha' in April 1566

successors.note: The Maona page: Piyale Pasha 'annexed Chios to the Ottoman Empire'.

capitals.name: Chios (Kastro)
capitals.note: Page silent on a capital; the castle of Chios town is the Genoese fleet's target in 1346 and its surrender on 12 September is the founding act.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row): the island of Chios. The Maona's title names 'Chios and the port of Phocaea' (Foça), but the page does not say what happened to Phocaea and the Foça page is silent on the Maona; Phocaea is therefore not drawn. No area on the page.

ledger.note: 12 September 1346: the Genoese take the castle of Chios. 'In 1346 a Genoese chartered company, the Maona, was set up in Genoa to reconquer and exploit Chios.' A Genoese fleet led by Simone Vignoso 'besieged the castle, which surrendered on 12 September'; the page does not repeat the year with the date. The Maona page's agreement between the Commune and its creditors is dated 26 February 1347 ('the association took the name Maona of Chios'), after 'a failed uprising in 1347' the Latins kept control.

April 1566: the Ottomans take Chios. 'The Mahona of Chios ended its activities in 1566 when the Turks invaded and occupied the island'; the Chios page: 'captured by the Ottoman Empire after the surrender to Piyale Pasha' in April 1566.
1566: the Maona of Chios ends after 220 years. 'Chios stayed in [the Giustiniani's] hands until the Turkish conquest' (Maona page).

wars.name: Genoese conquest of Chios
wars.outcome: Simone Vignoso's Genoese fleet besieged the castle, which surrendered on 12 September 1346; a Greek uprising failed in 1347 and the Latins kept control; the Maona (a company of creditors) was formed on 26 February 1347.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Chios
wars.outcome: Piyale Pasha's fleet took Chios in April 1566 and annexed it to the Ottoman Empire.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the border. Phocaea, named in the Maona title, is not drawn because no page opened dates it.

sources.title: Maona of Chios
sources.note: Name, 1346-1566, the 26 February 1347 agreement, Giustiniani, 1363 tribute, 1566.

sources.title: Chios
sources.note: 1346 expedition, 12 September surrender, 1347 uprising, April 1566 Ottoman capture.

sources.title: Foça
sources.note: Opened for Phocaea: thin on the Maona period; Genoese fief from the Byzantine emperor in 1275.

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row; slug free. Three pages opened. Not settled: (1) Phocaea: the Maona's title includes it but no page gives the years (the Foça page is silent on the Maona and on the Ottoman capture date), so it is left out; Samos, Ikaria and Oinousses are not mentioned for this period; (2) the date of the Giustiniani takeover of the Maona (the 'New Maona') is not on the pages; (3) the 1363 tribute to John V Palaiologos (Maona page) is not territorial; (4) the status is a Genoese company, a colony of the Republic of Genoa drawn in Genoa's tint (type colony, family italy); republic-of-genoa is Cliopatria's Genoa (1010-1795). No area on any page.
